title: Research snapshot: supply chains and ethical sourcing for inventors

sources.public: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026, SEC filings, news reports, and company websites. URLs are in docs/index.html.
sources.sayari: Sayari Graph (subscription). Entity links require a Sayari login.

evidence_levels.confirmed: A named source states the link between these two organizations or sites.
evidence_levels.likely: Evidence points to the link, but a source does not establish it for this specific step, or the goods were not verified.
evidence_levels.unknown: This project has not established the supplier. A gap is not evidence that a chain is clean or risky.

caveats: A link describes organizations. It does not prove what is inside a particular battery.
No researched chain reaches from a mine to a supplier that clearly serves small orders. The full chain ends at American Battery Solutions, which builds packs for industrial and commercial mobility.
Prices, minimum orders, delivery times, and shipping coverage are mostly unpublished. The site leaves them out unless a source states them.
Distance is measured from the center of the visitor's country and is not a delivery estimate.
Sayari company-name filters on shipment searches returned unrelated records and were not used as evidence. Entity relationships were used instead.
Sayari screening flags were not published. Many battery exporters carry product-level flags based on HS code and country, which are leads rather than findings about a company.
Small-order labels reflect what a source says. "Shop" means an online shop sells individual products, not that every item ships everywhere.
Marketplaces such as Xometry and Craftcloud may have parts made elsewhere, so the place shown is the company, not the factory.
The project owner confirmed that Sayari data can be used. Accuracy rules still apply, so unverified serious links stay off the site.

unconnected_leads.detail: Talison Lithium operates the mine. Albemarle owns 49%, and the Tianqi and IGO joint venture owns 51%. Each side can take 50% of output, and Talison names the Kwinana and Kemerton plants as downstream uses. No link from those plants to a cell maker has been established.
Komatsu agreed in November 2023 to acquire American Battery Solutions.

open_questions: Which cell makers supply Cell Pack Solutions, Epec, Akku Power, and Adafruit?
Which companies supply cobalt and nickel to LG Energy Solution, and in which cells?
Which pack makers will actually quote an inventor for 1 to 100 units, and in which countries?
Where do the metals in circuit boards, motors, and machined parts come from for each supplier?
coverage_note: Batteries have the deepest research. Other categories list real suppliers, mostly with raw material sources not established.

ethics_method.limits: This research cannot prove that any part was ethically sourced, and it does not rate companies as ethical or unethical.
ethics_method.materials: Mine production comes from USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026 (2025 estimates). Materials per category are typical and vary by product.
ethics_method.labor_evidence: Entries come from U.S. Department of Labor publications. The 2024 list was read through search results and official pages, not row by row, so entries are examples and the list of flagged countries is not complete. A listing does not mean all production in a country is affected or that a listed supplier uses that material.

supplier_levels.audit: An independent audit of a site
supplier_levels.report: A published report on due diligence
supplier_levels.parent: Policy found only from a parent company
supplier_levels.listed: A document is listed but was not read
supplier_levels.none: Nothing found in a web search in November 2026; this is not evidence of poor sourcing

labor_entries.Cobalt: Congo (Kinshasa): child labor since 2009; forced labor reported
labor_entries.Tin: Congo (Kinshasa): listed in 2024; Indonesia: child labor in earlier editions, 2024 status not confirmed
labor_entries.Tantalum: Congo (Kinshasa): child and forced labor in the 2018 edition; forced mining reported in 2024
labor_entries.Gold: Many countries, including Congo (Kinshasa) and Zimbabwe
labor_entries.Lithium-ion batteries: China: downstream listing based on mineral inputs
labor_entries.Not confirmed: Manganese and iron appear on the list, but country entries were not confirmed. No entry was seen for nickel, graphite, or rare earths; that is not evidence of no risk.

sayari_review.method: Records were matched by name, place, and identifiers. Trade partners and ownership were reviewed for selected suppliers, not all of them.
published: Likely trade links: PKCELL to Adafruit, General Lithium to LG Energy Solution, Adafruit to Macfos (Robu.in)
Company ownership for Cell Pack Solutions, Mouser, and Goodfellow
sayari_review.not_published: Risk flags, individual owners, and serious trade links where the goods could not be seen.
sayari_review.caveat: Shipment name filters returned unrelated records, so the goods behind these links are unverified.

source_dating.note: Publication dates are shown on the site for each source. Sources from 2023 or earlier are marked older. Some sources were read in full, and some were seen only as search excerpts.
source_dating.correction: The Proto Labs conflict minerals report cited covers 2024, not 2025.

risk_levels.method: One point each for a Department of Labor entry, conflict minerals coverage, and one country mining 50% or more. Two or more points is higher attention, and one is some attention.
risk_levels.applies_to: Materials, never companies. This is the project's own method, not a government rating or legal advice.
